title: Polyamines buffer labile iron to suppress ferroptosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO series GSE300179 (linked from PubMed): downloaded GSE300179_RAW.tar (1.1 MB), which holds two raw sgRNA (guide RNA) count files, DFMO_14d and Untreated_14d. Each has 97,888 guide rows and the columns ID, Gene and one count column. There are only 2 samples and no replicates. A third file, GSE300179_sgRNAs_seq.txt.gz, was listed but not opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract: a genome-wide CRISPR screen, an iron reporter and live-cell imaging. Europe PMC full text returned an error (HTTP 500), and the supplement was not retrievable. Any imaging or metabolomics data is not deposited anywhere I found.

a1_downloadable.note: The GEO count files downloaded freely; checked in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no gene-level fitness or synthetic-lethality score column. One would have to be built from raw counts of one treated sample versus one control. Checked in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene symbols and guide IDs are present; guide sequences are in a separate file.

a4_units_stated.note: The values are raw read counts.

a5_enough_rows.note: 97,888 guides (about 20k genes) but n=1 per condition: one phenotype contrast with no replicates, so there is nothing to generalise across.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without the full text; the two files agree with each other at 97,888 rows.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any label would be a log fold change computed by us from a single, unreplicated pair of counts. That is a noisy derived quantity, not a measured outcome.

integration.partner_dataset: DepMap (genome-wide CRISPR gene dependency across ~1,100 cell lines)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do genes that score as polyamine-dependent also show ferroptosis-linked dependency patterns across cancer cell lines? With n=1 here, this would be a correlation check, not an ML project.

controls.positive_control: GPX4 (glutathione peroxidase 4) should drop out under DFMO, as the abstract reports.

honest_claim_h3: Within one cell line and one unreplicated DFMO (a polyamine-synthesis inhibitor) versus control contrast, these genes changed in guide abundance. That is a hit list, not a training set.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene features to predict which gene knockouts become lethal when cells lose polyamines.
plain_idea.train_on: About 20,000 genes, each scored from guide-RNA counts in one treated and one untreated sample (97,888 guides verified).
plain_idea.predict: A per-gene drop in guide abundance under polyamine depletion, computed from raw counts with no replicates.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It could flag ferroptosis (iron-driven cell death) partners of polyamine therapy, but a single unreplicated screen can't support a model.

ml_idea: None viable: the only deposited data is a two-sample, unreplicated CRISPR screen. This is a mechanism paper, not a dataset paper.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the file sizes I opened; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the samples per condition in GSE300179. Done: 1 versus 1, so the project is dead.

verdict_reason: The only public data is one unreplicated treated-versus-control CRISPR screen (2 count files, 97,888 guides). Any label must be computed by us from n=1 per condition (A2/A8), and there is no table of measured outcomes to learn from.
